claims.text: A high-entropy-alloy-core, ultrathin Pt-rich-shell catalyst will enhance HER and HOR catalytic activity relative to conventional pure Pt catalysts.
The proposed core–shell catalyst will substantially improve durability under acidic potential-cycling conditions relative to conventional pure Pt catalysts.
A compositionally optimized, potentially refractory HEA core has superior structural durability.
The HEA core by itself has suboptimal intrinsic HER and HOR activity.
Depositing a nanoscale Pt-rich layer onto an HEA core creates the proposed core–shell nanoparticles.
The Pt-rich shell provides the catalytically active surface sites.
The HEA core provides mechanical and chemical stability.
A thin Pt-rich shell has high intrinsic catalytic activity for both HER and HOR.
The tunable composition and structural robustness of the HEA core mitigate catalyst degradation during acidic potential cycling.
Synergy at the Pt-rich-shell/HEA-core interface minimizes leaching relative to pure Pt.
Synergy at the Pt-rich-shell/HEA-core interface minimizes structural reconfiguration relative to pure Pt.
Reduced leaching and structural reconfiguration enhance long-term catalyst durability.
The proposed catalyst will exhibit initial current density and overpotential comparable to those of pure Pt.
The proposed catalyst will have a significantly lower performance-degradation rate than pure Pt during long-term cycling.
Conventional pure Pt catalysts are highly active for HER and HOR.
Conventional pure Pt catalysts suffer durability problems under prolonged and cyclic electrochemical operation.
Large deviations in HEA-core composition or synthesis conditions can compromise the core–shell interface.
Reproducibly synthesizing uniformly coated HEA-core/Pt-rich-shell nanoparticles may be challenging.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis states that catalytic activity will be enhanced relative to pure Pt, whereas the predicted outcome only expects activity comparable to pure Pt.
